messages.message:
Patch Set 1:

(6 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Some concerns, see inline comments. This now applies the PM-QoS request to up to two cpts on every successful send, including server-side AST sends, so on a busy node most of the machine ends up held at `pmqos_latency_max_usec`; it would help to state what that costs in idle residency, and whether the requester-side kick wants its own tunable rather than riding on `enable_pmqos`.

commit.subject: LU-20661 ptlrpc: also lower CPU latency on the requester cpt
commit.message:
LU-20661 ptlrpc: also lower CPU latency on the requester cpt

kick_cpu_latency() only lowered the latency of the cpt selected
by the target NID, which runs the LND scheduler threads, but not
the cpt of the thread woken up on reply. The thread that actually
consumes the reply (the caller for a sync RPC, a ptlrpcd for an
async one) is left on a deep C-state, limiting the benefit of the
PM QoS request. Split the per-cpt work into kick_cpt_latency()
and call it for the requester cpt as well when it differs from
the peer cpt.

Fixes: 54a64ea818d9 ("LU-18446 ptlrpc: lower CPUs latency during client I/O")
Signed-off-by: Xiao Yang <xyang@ddn.com>
Change-Id: Ic2e051c4f1fe78e1c55fd1d2688e15a4579567a3
